title: What Is Hypocrisy According To The Bible
paragraphs: Understanding Hypocrisy in the Light of Scripture

Hypocrisy is a concept that the Bible addresses with strong language and clear warnings. At its core, biblical hypocrisy refers to the act of presenting oneself as righteous or godly while inwardly lacking true devotion or integrity. The term comes from the Greek word "hypokrites," which originally referred to an actor—someone who wears a mask. In Scripture, hypocrisy is not merely failing to live up to one’s ideals (something all believers struggle with), but deliberately pretending to have virtues, moral beliefs, or religious devotion that one does not truly possess.
Jesus’ Condemnation of Hypocrisy
No one spoke against hypocrisy more forcefully than Jesus. His most pointed rebukes were directed at the religious leaders of His day, who outwardly appeared righteous but were inwardly corrupt.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness. - Matthew 23:27 ASV

Jesus exposes the heart of hypocrisy: the desire to appear righteous before others while neglecting true inner transformation. Elsewhere, He warns against practicing religious acts—such as giving, praying, and fasting—for the sake of being seen by others:
Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them: else ye have no reward with your Father who is in heaven. - Matthew 6:1 ASV
Here, Jesus teaches that even good works can become hypocrisy if they are motivated by the desire for human approval rather than love for God.
Old Testament Roots
The problem of hypocrisy is not new. The Old Testament prophets also confronted the people of Israel for going through the motions of worship while their hearts were far from God.
This people draw nigh unto me with their mouth, and honor me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. - Isaiah 29:13 ASV
True worship, according to Scripture, must flow from a sincere and devoted heart.
The Danger for All Believers
The Bible makes it clear that hypocrisy is a temptation for everyone. The apostle Paul warns Peter when he acts inconsistently with the gospel, showing that even leaders can fall into hypocrisy.
And the rest of the Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that even Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation. - Galatians 2:13 ASV
Here, “dissimulation” is another word for hypocrisy. Paul’s confrontation reminds us that the church must strive for integrity and authenticity in all things.
God’s Desire for Authentic Faith
Instead of hypocrisy, God desires sincerity and truth from His people. He calls believers to examine their hearts and walk in the light.

If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in the darkness, we lie, and do not the truth: but if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanseth us from all sin. - 1 John 1:6-7 ASV
This passage underlines the call to honest living—confessing sin, seeking forgiveness, and living transparently before God and others.
The Gospel Remedy for Hypocrisy

The only true remedy for hypocrisy is the gospel. Salvation by grace through faith in Jesus Christ changes the heart, not just outward behavior. Believers are called to genuine repentance and transformation through the indwelling Holy Spirit.
Therefore if any man is in Christ, he is a new creature: the old things are passed away; behold, they are become new. - 2 Corinthians 5:17 ASV
By continually turning to Christ, believers can resist the pull of hypocrisy and grow in sincere, authentic faith.
Conclusion

Hypocrisy is a serious issue in the Bible, described as a spiritual blindness that can infect even the most religious people. Scripture warns against external shows of religion without inward reality. The call is to live honestly before God, grounded in the grace and truth of Jesus Christ, so that our lives reflect the gospel both inside and out.
